discoveries: (1) The current usage line is fixed text, so argparse's options list will show the new options while the usage line will not, unless the text is edited; the usage cases check that line only. (2) A bad option makes the top-level parser print `usage: gov [-h] <command> ...`; only a missing role or ticket prints the launch usage line, so the "bad call" case uses that. (3) Values starting with `-` are left out of the form cases, because argparse would end those runs with exit 2 before the launcher sees them. (4) An unknown word after `--` reaches the CLI unchanged; W2-60a refuses only its listed arguments (e.g. `--no-chrome` passes).
